Daily price import format

Prepare a JSON file for Prices → Import daily price data → Import price data. A successful import immediately replaces the current imported batch. It stays in that tab until reload. A rejected file keeps the previous data. Keep your original file.

Synthetic format example

Every value, symbol and timestamp in this example is invented. It is format practice, not historical or current market data. It has no verified source, calendar, action coverage or hosted chart mapping.

The complete JSON is below. Copy it into a UTF-8 text file with a .json extension to practice the format. Reading this page does not import anything. Keep the app open in its original tab.

Fields to prepare

One daily series
FormatschemaVersion: "cribscore-price-series-v1", a distinct id, uppercase symbol, and three-letter currency.
Sessionsinterval: "1d", an IANA sessionTimezone such as America/New_York, and each exchange-local session date as YYYY-MM-DD.
PricesQuoted ordinary decimal strings for open, high, low, close. Keep the source precision; do not convert to binary floating-point first. High and low must contain open and close.
VolumeA number or null for unknown volume. Ordinary share volume must be a whole number; split-adjusted volume may be fractional. Declare volumeBasis as shares, split_adjusted_shares or unknown.
SourceNonempty source.provider and source.dataset, with channel: "manual_import". Use null for an unknown url, capturedAt, publishedAt, responseSha256 or declaredDelayMinutes. A known URL must be HTTPS and contain no credentials. A known digest is 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.
AdjustmentspriceBasis is unadjusted, split_adjusted, total_return_adjusted or unknown. Use what the source establishes. Use actions.status: "unknown" and items: [] when action coverage has not been established. An empty list does not certify that no actions occurred.

Optional originalSymbol, entityId and exchange retain source identity when known; they can be omitted or null. The table and price highlight preserve canonical decimal strings; insignificant trailing zeros may disappear. The plot and indexed comparisons are approximate. You need not create the generated decimals fields yourself. If re-importing a normalized file, keep its numeric and decimal fields consistent.

Keep the clocks separate

capturedAt is the actual source retrieval time. publishedAt is a separately known publication time. Use exact UTC timestamps with seconds and Z, optionally 1–3 fractional digits. Publication must not follow capture. Keep unknown nullable metadata null; keep original clocks when importing later.

If you supply a bar availableAt, it must be a valid UTC timestamp, no earlier than known publication and no later than known capture; an invalid value rejects the file. If it is omitted or null, the parser uses capture, then known publication, or leaves availability unknown. A session date alone is not a quote timestamp.

Coverage and trust remain explicit

Imports do not provide a verified exchange calendar. A continuous line does not establish holidays, early closes or missing-session coverage. A recent capture does not establish current prices; unknown delay is not zero. An empty action list does not establish that no splits or dividends occurred.

Imported data is chart context only. Import success does not verify source rights or account entitlement, create a paper trade, supply journal marks or change rankings. TradingView is a separate display. Raw provider responses, including Alpaca bars, need conversion to this format with their original source metadata. Importing them does not connect or authenticate a provider account.

Limits and multiple companies

The upload UI accepts JSON only: at most 2 MiB, 16 series, 5,000 bars per series and 40,000 bars total. Session dates must be unique per series; IDs and symbols must be unique per batch. Duplicate JSON keys are rejected. Positive prices support up to 12 decimal places and a maximum value of 1000000000000. Ordinary decimal strings cannot contain commas, currency signs or exponents.

To retain several companies together, put their complete objects in the series array of a wrapper with schemaVersion: "cribscore-price-import-v1". Each successful upload replaces the previous batch. CSV is not accepted by this form.

Inspect the complete synthetic JSON
{
  "schemaVersion": "cribscore-price-series-v1",
  "id": "synthetic-guide-example",
  "symbol": "DEMO",
  "originalSymbol": "DEMO",
  "entityId": null,
  "currency": "USD",
  "exchange": "SYNTHETIC",
  "sessionTimezone": "America/New_York",
  "interval": "1d",
  "priceBasis": "unadjusted",
  "volumeBasis": "shares",
  "source": {
    "provider": "SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE — not market data",

    "capturedAt": "2020-01-08T22:00:00Z",
    "publishedAt": null,
    "responseSha256": null,
